comparison: Perfect alignment on background/context claims C1-C8. Both recognize these as establishing scientific rationale with appropriate citations to prior work. No disagreement on the foundational context.

High concordance on RNA-seq findings (C17-C26). OpenEval emphasizes technical rigor (N=3 donors, FDR<0.05) and biological validation through pathway enrichment. Peer reviewers accept the expression dynamics and request comparison context with other studies, which was addressed in revision.

Both support chromatin accessibility findings (C27-C32). OpenEval highlights statistical thresholds and biological coherence of stable TADs with dynamic local accessibility. Peer reviewers accept findings after authors included comparative data from other studies.

Strong agreement on HiC analysis quality (C39-C43). OpenEval emphasizes sequencing depth and 40% concordance with prior pcHiC as validation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge prior pcHiC work and accept the comparative analysis after comprehensive revision.

Both support comprehensive HiC findings (C33-C38). OpenEval details technical quality (4 billion reads, Fit-HiC2) and integration with gene expression. Peer reviewers praise intensive analysis of chromatin architecture data for disease SNP discovery.

Agreement on TF footprinting methodology (C44-C50). OpenEval validates HINT-ATAC approach and integration with expression data. Peer reviewers accept TF footprinting findings when contextualized with prior studies, requesting comparison of enriched TFs across datasets.

Both support regulatory network findings (C52-C54). OpenEval notes identification of known factors validates approach while novel factors represent new hypotheses. Peer reviewers accept network analysis without challenge, consistent with overall transcriptional profiling acceptance.

Strong concordance on disease enrichment (C61-C64). OpenEval highlights partitioned LD score regression validation. Peer reviewers accept the work as 'useful additional resource' and praise intensive analysis for autoimmune disease SNP discovery.

Agreement on V2G mapping characteristics (C68-C73). OpenEval emphasizes variants are 103kb from targets, contact multiple genes, and skip nearest gene. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'Most of these were not in the proximal promoter, but rather distal enhancers.'

Both support core V2G methodology (C9-C11, C60, C65-C66). OpenEval details credible set reduction from 14 to 3 variants. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as core finding, with Reviewer 1 noting 'over a 1000 genes physically linked' and Reviewer 3 confirming '423 GWAS signals to their respective target genes.'

Both support specific V2G examples (C74-C75). OpenEval provides technical details (PP>0.99 for rs1077667) and validates gene functions with citations. Peer reviewers accept these as illustrative proof-of-concept for dynamic variant-gene connections.

Strong agreement on low concordance between V2G approaches (C84-C91). OpenEval notes concern but suggests genuine biological differences between methods. Peer reviewers initially concerned but accept after expanded discussion provides 'framework to help explain inherent differences between these methods.'

Both address comparison with prior work (C80-C83). OpenEval describes systematic harmonization and statistical validation. Peer reviewers acknowledge prior pcHiC studies and accept comparative analysis after comprehensive revision.

Agreement on precision-recall benchmarking (C92-C98). OpenEval details threefold improvement with HiC and superior performance vs eQTL/ABC, but notes low 16% recall. Peer reviewers accept framework with caveats about sample size, noting expanded discussion addresses limitations.

Strong concordance on ABC comparison (C99-C102). OpenEval highlights ABC limitations. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly praises this as 'Most significantly' contribution, stating authors 'outlined the key limitations of ABC relative to their method.'

Unanimous strong support for IL2 enhancer characterization (C107-C114). OpenEval details multiple lines of evidence (conservation, GWAS, ATAC-seq, HiC, ChIP-seq, reporter assays). All peer reviewers explicitly praise this work as 'impressive,' 'Most compelling,' and a key strength.

Strong agreement on CRISPR validation (C115-C122). OpenEval notes consistent effects across cell types and dramatic phenotype of large deletion. Peer reviewers praise functional validation showing enhancers 'functionally shown to be important in regulating IL-2 expression.'

Perfect alignment on memory T cell findings (C123-C125). OpenEval supports differential accessibility patterns and epigenetic memory inference. Peer reviewers accept this as extension of praised IL2 work without challenge.

Strong concordance on mouse in vivo validation (C126-C140). OpenEval details sequence/functional conservation and in vivo phenotypes with appropriate controls. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly highlights this as strength, noting enhancers 'functionally shown to be important' including 'susceptibility to colitis.'

Agreement on allelic effects (C141). OpenEval describes reporter assays (N=7 donors) showing functional effects. Peer Reviewer 3 states 'distal enhancers harboring disease relevant SNPs, which were shown to affect IL-2 transcription,' explicitly supporting this finding.

Perfect alignment on CRISPR screen validation (C143-C147). OpenEval notes statistically significant enrichments with modest magnitude (~30% for IMPC). Peer reviewers explicitly accept this validation, with Reviewer 1 noting 'enrichments for regulators' and Reviewer 3 confirming 'novel genes were identified.'

Strong agreement on pharmacological validation (C148-C150). OpenEval notes 6/9 success rate as strong support with appropriate caveats for failures. Peer reviewers accept validation, with Reviewer 1 noting inhibition 'impacts T cell activation' and Reviewer 3 supporting novel gene discovery.

Agreement on V2G approach differences (C152-C156). OpenEval emphasizes most V2G genes are not nearest gene, challenging simple assumptions. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms 'Most of these were not in the proximal promoter, but rather distal enhancers,' accepting low concordance explanations.

Perfect alignment on methodological comparisons (C160-C167). OpenEval details technical differences and cell type coverage limitations. Peer Reviewer 1 thanks authors for 'comprehensive comparative analysis' and discussion of 'potential sources of differences,' indicating acceptance.

OpenEval provides historical context for HIEI truth set (C168-C170) to interpret low recall rates. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though context is relevant to precision-recall analysis accepted by reviewers.

OpenEval describes validation of specific V2G genes with pharmacological data (C172-C185), including striking pM potency for SIK1 inhibitor. No specific peer review evaluation of these individual gene validations, though overall pharmacological approach is accepted by reviewers.

Both address study summary claims (C10-C11). OpenEval notes these accurately reflect major contributions supported by experimental evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge core findings about gene-variant linkage, with overlap on summary statements about V2G methodology.
